also: go back and forth to work

terms.gloss: go to and fro; come into a place regularly
terms.grammar: intransitive; with in and the accusative of the place, or inter … et …; often with ultrō citrōque
evidence: Ter. Hec. 175: hūc rārō in urbem commeat
Liv. 5.47: inter Vejōs Rōmamque nūntiōs commeāre
terms.comment: The classical verb for going regularly to and fro between two places, and for coming often to a place: what a commuter does. The commuter is quī cotīdiē in urbem commeat.

evidence: Varr. RR 3.5.16: pisciculī ultrō ac citrō commeant (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: nam senex rūs abdidit sē, hūc rārō in urbem commeat
phrases.english: for the old man has buried himself in the country; he seldom comes into town

phrases.latin: Decem septem mīlibus passuum ab urbe sēcessit, ut perāctīs quae agenda fuerint salvō jam et compositō diē possīs ibi manēre.
phrases.english: It lies seventeen miles from the city, so that when you have done what had to be done, you can stay there with your day still whole and in order.

phrases.latin: Multī cotīdiē in urbem commeant; pater domī labōrat.
phrases.english: Lots of people commute into town every day; Daddy works at home.

sources: Lewis & Short: commeo · Lewis & Short: ultro · Lewis & Short: citro
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. commute, shuttle.
